Class StorageAttachment<O,C>

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.containers.api.storage.StorageAttachment<O,C>
Type Parameters:
O - owner type (Void for ephemeral, Player, BlockEntity and so on for the persistent variants)
C - content type: a NonNullList of ItemStack for most factories, ItemContainerContents for itemContainer(int), and consumer-defined for custom specs
Direct Known Subclasses:
StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment
public abstract class StorageAttachment<O,C> extends Object
Where a slot group's contents are saved, by owner type.

Each factory gives a Storage bound to one owner. The storage reads and writes wherever the factory keeps its data: a Fabric attachment (player, block entity, entity), a data component (item stack), an in-memory list (ephemeral), or consumer-supplied hooks (CustomAttachmentSpec).

Usage

// At mod init, declare the attachment.
public static final StorageAttachment<BlockEntity, NonNullList<ItemStack>> FURNACE_EXTRA =
    StorageAttachment.blockScoped("my-mod", "furnace_extra", 1);

// At menu construction, bind to a specific owner instance.
Storage storage = FURNACE_EXTRA.bind(furnaceBE);
panel.slotGroup("extra").slot(0, 0).build(storage);

    • bind

      public abstract Storage bind(O owner)
      Binds this attachment to one owner, returning a Storage that reads and writes the content for that owner.

      Owners whose reference stays the same while the menu is open (Player, BlockEntity, Entity) are passed directly.

    • bind

      public Storage bind(Supplier<O> ownerSupplier)
      Binds through a supplier, for owners whose reference can change while the menu is open (notably ItemStack, which vanilla may replace during interactions). The supplier is called on every read and write.

    • ephemeral

      public static StorageAttachment<Void, net.minecraft.core.NonNullList<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack>> ephemeral(int slotCount)
      In-memory storage that lasts only while the menu is open. Its content is lost when the menu closes unless the handler's close-drop rule catches it. The same as wrapping an EphemeralStorage, through the common API.

      Owner type is Void; callers pass null to bind(O).

    • playerAttached

      public static StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment<net.minecraft.core.NonNullList<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack>> playerAttached(String namespace, String path, int slotCount)
      Saves slot-group content on a Player in a Fabric attachment. The content stays with the player across sessions and dimensions.

      Death handling

      Player content attachments start at DropRule.DEFAULT, which matches vanilla with no setup. On death the content drops at the death spot when keepInventory is off (Curse of Vanishing destroys it instead), and is kept across respawn when keepInventory is on. Change it per attachment with dropsOnDeath(DropRule), for example KEEP for a soulbound slot. The attachment registers copyOnDeath so kept content carries across respawn, and the library does the gamerule-gated drop.
      Parameters:
      namespace - attachment-id namespace (consumer's mod id)
      path - attachment-id path (unique per consumer-declared attachment)
      slotCount - number of item slots the content holds

    • blockScoped

      public static StorageAttachment<net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity, net.minecraft.core.NonNullList<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack>> blockScoped(String namespace, String path, int slotCount)
      Saves slot-group content on a BlockEntity in a Fabric attachment. The content lives as long as the block: breaking it destroys the attachment and drops the content, as for a vanilla container. For containers that go with their block (chest, furnace, hopper and so on).
      Parameters:
      namespace - attachment-id namespace (consumer's mod id)
      path - attachment-id path (unique per consumer-declared attachment)
      slotCount - number of item slots the content holds

    • entityAttached

      public static StorageAttachment<net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity, net.minecraft.core.NonNullList<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack>> entityAttached(String namespace, String path, int slotCount)
      Saves slot-group content on any Entity in a Fabric attachment. The content is saved in the entity's NBT and goes when the entity does, with nothing carried over (unlike playerAttached(String, String, int), which has death handling). For containers owned by an entity: a minecart with chest, a donkey, llama or mule, or other entity-scoped slots.

      Saved on the server. The menu's vanilla slot protocol keeps the client view current (the registered slots write the client-side attachment on each ContainerSetSlot), the same way playerAttached(String, String, int) content shows without a separate attachment sync.

      Parameters:
      namespace - attachment-id namespace (consumer's mod id)
      path - attachment-id path (unique per consumer-declared attachment)
      slotCount - number of item slots the content holds

    • itemContainer

      public static StorageAttachment<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack, net.minecraft.world.item.component.ItemContainerContents> itemContainer(int slotCount)
      Saves slot-group content on an ItemStack in vanilla's DataComponents.CONTAINER component (ItemContainerContents). The content travels with the item through menus, pickup, dropping and throwing.

      Always uses DataComponents.CONTAINER, the component vanilla uses for item-backed contents (shulker items, bundles). A generic itemAttached(DataComponentType<C>, ...) factory can come later if a consumer needs a different component.

      Vanilla can replace an ItemStack during interactions (when a slot is emptied, for example), so prefer bind(Supplier) over bind(Object) for item-backed storage.

    • custom

      public static <O,C> StorageAttachment<O,C> custom(CustomAttachmentSpec<O,C> spec)
      Wraps a CustomAttachmentSpec as a StorageAttachment. For owner types the built-in factories don't cover, and for consumers whose save and load don't go through a MenuKit handler.

      This is the non-player path: the returned StorageAttachment has no dropsOnDeath, because death handling is player-only. For a player-anchored custom spec that needs death handling, use customPlayerAttached(CustomAttachmentSpec), which returns a StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment.

      Type Parameters:
      O - owner type
      C - content type

    • customPlayerAttached

      public static <C> StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment<C> customPlayerAttached(CustomAttachmentSpec<net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player, C> spec)
      Wraps a player-anchored CustomAttachmentSpec as a StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment, so it can opt in to death handling with StorageAttachment.PlayerStorageAttachment.dropsOnDeath(DropRule). The spec's owner type must be Player, which the typed factory checks at compile time (the old base dropsOnDeath threw at runtime on a non-player spec).

      The library does the gamerule-gated DROP/DESTROY at the death site. Keeping items across respawn is up to the consumer's storage: set copyOnDeath on your Fabric attachment, or use a persistent store. The library can't set copyOnDeath on storage it does not own, which is the point of a custom spec.

      Type Parameters:
      C - content type
